findings.evidence: New file 109-115 `structure IsElasticStabilizer ... isometry : Bilin.IsIsometry g f / fixes_left : f p = p / fixes_right : f p' = p'` vs `Tensors/Basic.lean:523-530` `structure IsKinematicStabilizer ... isometry : Bilin.IsIsometry g f / fixes_p : f K.p = K.p / fixes_q : f K.q = K.q`; new 144-147 proof terms `Bilin.reflect_isometry g hSymm u hu`, `Bilin.reflect_apply_of_orthogonal g u p hup/hup'` are identical to `Tensors/Basic.lean:571-574`. Grep shows `IsKinematicStabilizer` occurs only in `Tensors/Basic.lean` (lines 523, 535, 539, 546, 571, 863, 1140, 1168), so the generalisation is confined to one file.
findings.fix: Define the stabiliser of a vector pair once at the `Bilin` level in `Tensors/Basic.lean` (next to `IsIsometry`/`reflect`), e.g. `Bilin.IsStabilizer g a b f` with one `Bilin.reflect_isStabilizer`, replace the eight in-file uses of `IsKinematicStabilizer` (all inside `Tensors/Basic.lean`) with `Bilin.IsStabilizer g K.p K.q`, and have this module's covariance section use the same notion rather than a second copy (drop `Elastic` from the name, since the definitions are mass-agnostic).
findings.issue: `IsElasticStabilizer` (109-115) and `reflect_isElasticStabilizer` (142-147) duplicate `Tensors.Hadronic.IsKinematicStabilizer` and `reflect_isKinematicStabilizer`; the only difference is that the two fixed vectors come as arguments instead of out of a `DisKinematics`. Nothing in `IsElasticStabilizer`, `IsCovariant`, `isCovariant_smul_add_smul`, `IsCovariant.apply_eq_zero`, `apply_sub_smul_add_smul` or `IsCovariant.existsUnique_eq_smul` mentions mesons, spin zero or form factors — they are statements about `g` and two vectors, and Layer 4's unequal-mass transition form factor will need exactly them.

findings.evidence: New 166-169 `span : ∀ v, ∃ a b u, g u p = 0 ∧ g u p' = 0 ∧ v = a • p + b • p' + u` / `anisotropic : ... → g u u ≠ 0` vs `Tensors/Basic.lean:853-858` `span : ∀ v, ∃ a b u, g K.q u = 0 ∧ g (pTransverse g K) u = 0 ∧ v = a • pTransverse g K + b • K.q + u` / `definite : ... → g u u < 0`.
findings.fix: Factor the pair-indexed part out at the `Bilin` level — `Bilin.IsOrthogonalSplitting g x y` with the `span` and `anisotropic` (`g u u ≠ 0`) fields — and let `Hadronic.SpectatorAssumptions` extend it with its stronger `definite` and its `transitive` field, with this module instantiating it at `(p, p')`.
findings.issue: Same problem a second time: `ElasticSpectatorAssumptions.span`/`anisotropic` repeats the span-plus-non-degeneracy inputs of `Hadronic.SpectatorAssumptions.span`/`definite` for the pair `(p, p')` instead of the pair `(p_T, q)`, so the library now carries two unrelated names for `{x, y}^⊥` splitting over the same `Bilin V`.

summary: The form-factor material (HasFormFactor, chargeRadiusSq, singlePole) sits at the natural level with minimal hypotheses, but the covariance machinery re-states existing DIS-tensor declarations one level below where they belong: the stabiliser structure and its reflection lemma are exact clones of the upstream kinematic versions, and the spectator-assumption structure repeats the same span/anisotropy shape for a different vector pair.
